source.title: Dynamical stability and chaos in artificial neural network trajectories along training
source.authors: Kaloyan Danovski; Miguel C. Soriano; Lucas Lacasa

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Reports gradient-descent classification results on Iris and MNIST, extending the training-success question to small sigmoid networks and different datasets. It does not test the listed CIFAR settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Iris training and testing accuracy in Figure 14, but supplies no exact values in the text. The MNIST accuracy results are for the test set, so they do not measure the training error in the claim. Other stability and loss-trajectory results do not directly measure the claim's training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study measures learning and trajectory dynamics in shallow sigmoid networks. It does not test V1's convolutional-network training-error claim or establish the stability thresholds and curvature behavior required by V5. Its use of the term edge of stability rests on analogy rather than measured sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the Iris performance examples and scope caveat, but omits the central conclusion: training viewed as a graph dynamical system exhibits nontrivial parameter-trajectory stability, sensitive dependence at intermediate learning rates, and intermittent-like dynamics at very large rates. These findings are exploratory; preliminary MNIST results suggest some similar behavior, while broader generality remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch gradient descent with constant learning rate, rather than SGD or Adam; one-hidden-layer sigmoid networks; Iris and a fixed subset of MNIST rather than CIFAR benchmarks. The tested claim's label corruption, width, and size comparisons are not studied.
record.method_sensitivity: The Iris task's reported learning outcome changes with learning rate: effective at η = 0.01 and η = 1, little learning at η = 5. The authors state that regime boundaries depend on the problem, architecture, and data.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report effective Iris classification learning at η = 0.01 and η = 1, but essentially random classification at η = 5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate choice affects classification learning in a one-hidden-layer sigmoid network trained with full-batch GD on Iris.

fits_no_version.finding: On Iris, η = 1 produces non-monotonic training loss that eventually approaches zero; η = 5 produces large, irregular loss without numerical divergence. MNIST also shows faster learning at intermediate rates. No stability threshold or Hessian sharpness is measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow sigmoid networks can learn with non-monotonic loss at some elevated learning rates, while still larger rates can impair learning without numerical divergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Nearby parameter trajectories can separate while loss falls; positive finite network Lyapunov exponents suggest sensitive dependence at intermediate learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convergence of training loss can coexist with divergence of nearby parameter trajectories.

record.code_released: https://github.com/GitKalo/ann dynamics (authors say data and code will be available upon publication)
record.problems: The paper uses a toy Iris task and a shallow network chosen for illustration. Iris accuracy results are presented in figures without exact values in the text; the performance examples are for single initial conditions. The authors say generalization across tasks and architectures remains to be studied.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-classification-error results were extracted. MNIST accuracy is reported for the test set, not training; loss trajectories and network-distance measurements do not directly measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100 using SGD or Adam, including label corruption and the stated size and recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention by residual shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparative initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Learning rates calibrated against the initial linearized stability limit; squared-loss recovery with curvature reduction; measured sharpness approaching and remaining near the full-batch stability threshold; divergence relative to those thresholds.
Batch-normalization comparisons and training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V1 verdicts. Failure at an extreme learning rate in a small Iris sigmoid network is not a counterexample to V1. The paper's discussion of Cohen et al.'s sharpness results is cited background, not its own measurement.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; convolutional networks; SGD or Adam; corrupted or random labels; model-size comparisons; early stopping and regularized recipes.

rows.subject: fully-connected, feed-forward neural network with a single hidden layer of 10 units
rows.stage_stated: trained from Gaussian random weights; biases initialized to zero
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on the Iris classification task; training accuracy reported.

conditions.value: Iris; fixed training set of 120 datapoints

rows.note: The authors state that the low learning-rate regime learned the classification task effectively. Figure 14 shows training accuracy, but the text gives no exact value.
rows.check: Iris training accuracy in a shallow sigmoid network trained with full-batch GD does not measure V1's specified effect. Effective learning also does not establish near-zero training error; Figure 14's accuracy values cannot be read from the supplied text.
